1→# PROJECT: Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→**Status: BUILT, IN POLISH (updated 2026-10-07).** The system runs end to end on the mock and on
   4→the real Tencent model; the application build freezes on **12 Oct 2026** (operator ruling), after
   5→which only recording, documentation and deploy work continue. Building started 2026-09-21. Planning closed **2026-09-19** and the scope, stack and
   6→workflow are ruled. This file is CodeBuddy's memory for this project: the builder's entry
   7→point. The ruled scope lives in
   8→the planning repository and is deliberately unreadable from here (the permission fence in
   9→`.codebuddy/settings.json` denies reads of that path, and it is verified to work), so
  10→**everything you need is in this file, `docs/` and the kickoff prompt the operator gives you**.
  11→If a session needs a fact that is neither here nor in the docs: stop and ask; do not invent
  12→scope.
  13→
  14→## What this project is
  15→
  16→Ryde track entry for the Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026. The challenge is a
  17→**multi-agent autonomous dispute resolution system** for ride-hailing disputes: a Rider Advocate
  18→agent, a Driver Advocate agent, and a Judge agent that weighs both cases, applies company policy and
  19→issues a ruling with a confidence score.
  20→
  21→`docs/statement-extract.md` holds the challenge statement verbatim. Read it before any build work.
  22→It is the requirements floor: the locked scope below is the team's chosen subset of it, and the
  23→locked scope never widens past the statement.
  24→
  25→## Hard requirements (non-negotiable)
  26→
  27→- The project must be **original** and built on **at least one of CodeBuddy or WorkBuddy**.
  28→- **Proof of product usage is mandatory.** Without it the project is **not scored at all**. Evidence
  29→  is screenshots of CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy chat logs, minimum three, accumulated as work happens. It
  30→  cannot be reconstructed later, so capture as you go.
  31→- The project must be **demoable end to end for at least two dispute categories**.
  32→- **Inter-agent communication must be observable** to a judge: a visible log or UI showing how the
  33→  agents exchange information and build their cases.
  34→- Deliverables include a public GitHub repo with complete source, an architecture diagram, and a live
  35→  demo walkthrough.
  36→- The repository is **PUBLIC**. Never commit credentials, API keys, tokens or personal data.
  37→
  38→## Locked build scope
  39→
  40→These decisions are ruled by the team and are **not open to re-litigation**:
  41→
  42→- **Categories:** route deviation + no-show charge, end to end. No third category.
  43→- **Agents:** exactly three decide each dispute — Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge. The
  44→  Judge always emits a confidence score (0–1). Below a configurable threshold it does not rule;
  45→  the parties see only a neutral "your case is still under review" message. Escalation is MVP, not stretch.
  46→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A fourth role, the **Policy & Precedent agent**, is a stretch item
  47→  built only if time allows: it reads human decisions and **proposes** policy changes, a human
  48→  approves or rejects each proposal, and it **never rules on a live case** and never edits the
  49→  policy or the code gates itself.
  50→- **Parties are spectators:** disputes arrive through a standardized intake form (category
  51→  dropdown; "other" routes to a human-review queue with a neutral message). The advocates screen
  52→  the submitted answers and may ask the party targeted follow-ups only when data conflicts or
  53→  is insufficient. No fourth intake agent. Parties never chat with the agents.
  54→- **Deterministic evidence layer:** all quantitative evidence (route deviation km/%, duration vs
  55→  estimate, fare recomputation, cancellation timestamps, chat-log signals, behaviour profile)
  56→  is computed in Python into a typed **Evidence Pack**. Agents may cite pack fields; they must
  57→  never do the arithmetic themselves.
  58→- **Policy as a swappable document:** `docs/policy.md`, rules with IDs and provenance stated
  59→  in the file. The Judge and advocates cite rule IDs. Policy text can be loaded from another
  60→  path, but it and the separately implemented Python safeguards must remain aligned; a text
  61→  replacement does not change the gates or their configured thresholds.
  62→- **Dataset as a swappable document:** synthesised corpus in `data/`, labelled with
  63→  ground-truth rulings (the correct ruling per case, by design) so replayed-run consistency is
  64→  measurable. Same swap rule.
  65→- **Observability surface (required by the statement):** a case-file view — each side's claim,
  66→  evidence and policy citations, with agent-to-agent traffic as a compact timestamped event
  67→  strip (full text one click deeper). This screen is the demo's home.
  68→- **Stack:** Python backend + plain HTML/JS front end. No heavy framework. The backend calls
  69→  Tencent Cloud's LLM API directly (key in `.env`, never committed). CodeBuddy writes the code;
  70→  it is never the runtime.
  71→- **Repo layout:** `app/` (Python backend), `ui/` (front end), `docs/` (architecture diagram,
  72→  policy set, dataset description), `evidence/` (development-process screenshots), `tools/` +
  73→  `tests/` (marked **non-app**: helper scripts and tests only; `app/` and `ui/` never import
  74→  from them). **The repo is PUBLIC at submission — never commit credentials or personal data.**
  75→- **Deployment:** local run for the live demo (real backend, real LLM calls). *(Amended
  76→  2026-10-01.)* The public link is a static replay on EdgeOne Pages of the **full loop** (filing →
  77→  the Judge withholds → a human decides → the party's status page), labelled honestly as a
  78→  replay of a real run with its date; it ships first. Optional polish on top: a hosted live
  79→  system behind one shared judge password (every page and API), a daily case cap and a daily
  80→  health check, with keys rotated before it goes up.
  81→
  82→## Non-negotiable engineering rules
  83→
  84→- Never commit `.env`, API keys, tokens, or any credential. The repo is public.
  85→- Do not read or write anything outside this folder — **this is a rule you must honour, not
  86→  something the fence guarantees.** The permission fence in `.codebuddy/settings.json` denies
  87→  reads of the planning repository path and of secret files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  88→  `secrets/`), denies `curl`, `wget`, `rm -rf` and `git push`, and asks before `git remote`.
  89→  It does NOT block other writes or other reads. Staying inside this folder is your job.
  90→- Verify work by running it, not by describing it. A feature is done when it has been exercised and
  91→  the real output checked.
  92→- Keep the demo path working at all times. A half-built stretch goal that breaks the main flow is
  93→  worse than no stretch goal.
  94→- **Only the CodeBuddy build lane writes `app/` and `ui/`.** Any other AI assistant used for
  95→  rescue or unblocking (e.g. another coding agent) is confined to `tools/` and `tests/` and must never
  96→  touch application code — the project's "built on CodeBuddy" claim must stay honest.
  97→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A defect that lives only in `app/` or `ui/` follows the normal path:
  98→  the planning agent writes a failing test and a brief, the CodeBuddy build lane fixes it (on
  99→  the default flash model), the planning agent verifies. **One exception:** within 48 hours of
 100→  the submission deadline, if the build lane cannot land a fix in time, the rescue lane may fix
 101→  it, and every such change is logged with its reason in the commit message and in
 102→  `docs/tool-experiences.md`.
 103→
 104→## How work is done here
 105→
 106→- **One capability at a time**, verified before moving on.
 107→- Commit with a clear message after each verified step.
 108→- Log decisions as they are made. A future session starts from these files, not from memory.
 109→- **Effort follows the Demo Day rubric:** 40 of 100 points are story, design and presentation,
 110→  so `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the demo walkthrough are deliverables on the same
 111→  footing as code — polished after the MVP floor is standing, never skipped.
 112→- **Run from this folder.** `cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build && codebuddy`. Sessions are
 113→  scoped by launch directory, and this folder carries its own memory file and permission fence.
 114→- **Default model is `deepseek-v4.1-flash`** (global default, x0.00 cost multiplier). Override per
 115→  task with `--model <id>` only when the work warrants the expense: GPT-5.6-Luna x0.14 is the cheap
 116→  upgrade, Kimi-K3 x1.62 for hard reasoning. Never use Primary, Deep, Sol or GPT-6-Astra here.
 117→- **Headless capture:** `codebuddy -p "<prompt>" --output-format json` returns machine-readable
 118→  results and writes a transcript to `~/.codebuddy/projects/`. Useful when the build needs to be
 119→  driven from outside the interactive session.
 120→
 121→## Layout
 122→
 123→```
 124→ryde-build/
 125→├── CODEBUDDY.md            # this file — project memory + locked scope
 126→├── README.md               # judge's entry point (judge-first: what it is → see it run → diagram)
 127→├── .codebuddy/
 128→│   └── settings.json       # permission fence
 129→├── app/                    # Python backend — agents, evidence layer, LLM calls, server, eval
 130→├── ui/                     # plain HTML/JS front end — operator console (case-file view)
 131→│   └── party/              # rider and driver intake forms, driver account, status page
 132→├── data/packs/             # two swappable dataset packs, ground-truth labelled:
 133→│                           #   organiser-style-v1 (default) and ryde-synth-v1
 134→├── docs/
 135→│   ├── statement-extract.md  # challenge statement, verbatim — the only requirements source
 136→│   ├── policy.md             # policy rule set (swappable; provenance stated in-file)
 137→│   ├── dataset.md            # dataset description + provenance
 138→│   ├── architecture.md       # required deliverable: diagram + system description
 139→│   ├── prompts.md            # how the prompts drive each agent
 140→│   ├── replay.md             # static replay export for the public link
 141→│   ├── evidence-plan.md      # §8 evidence rules and naming
 142→│   ├── tool-experiences.md   # running log of how the tools behaved
 143→│   └── build-briefs/         # one brief per build session, kept as a process record
 144→├── evidence/               # §8 screenshots (YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<topic>.png|.jpg)
 145→├── tools/                  # NON-APP helper scripts — app/ never imports from here
 146→│   └── replay/             # static replay page and its shim
 147→└── tests/                  # NON-APP tests (stdlib only)
 148→```
 149→
 150→New session briefs go in `docs/build-briefs/`. Do not create a document as a side effect of
 151→other work; each one is authored in the session whose brief names it.
 152→

  18→  [guided replay](https://ryde-dispute-replay.edgeone.dev/replay/) walks through one recorded

1→# Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→Entry for the **Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026**, Digital Native track
   4→(the Ryde challenge statement, section 5 of the organisers' document).
   5→
   6→**Status: the system runs end to end on the real Tencent Cloud model (ADP), with the
   7→deterministic mock as the default for a fresh checkout.** The scope is ruled: a two-category MVP
   8→(route deviation + no-show charge) with three agents, a deterministic evidence layer, and an
   9→observable case-file view. The challenge statement is in
  10→[`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md); the builder's contract is in
  11→[`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md).
  12→
  13→## Start here
  14→
  15→- **Try it online, nothing to install:** three copies are hosted on Tencent EdgeOne. The
  16→  [live AI site](https://ryde-dispute-live.edgeone.dev) runs the real Tencent model, with filings
  17→  limited per visitor and per day ([deploy notes](deploy/edgeone/README.md)). The
  18→  [practice site](https://ryde-dispute-demo.edgeone.dev) runs the deterministic mock. The
  19→  [guided replay](https://ryde-dispute-replay.edgeone.dev/replay/) walks through one recorded
  20→  real case from filing to human decision. Hosted cases are not permanent: an idle restart or a
  21→  redeploy clears them.
  22→- **Try it without a key:** [Run](#run). A new server from the standard launchers uses the deterministic mock; an existing Ryde server is reused as it is.
  23→- **Use approved Tencent access:** [Local live-copy guide](docs/live-copy.md). The live launchers are separate and need a private sidecar.
  24→- **Inspect the design:** [Architecture](docs/architecture.md), [policy](docs/policy.md) and [dataset](docs/dataset.md).
  25→- **Inspect development evidence:** [Conversation history](evidence/conversation-history/README.md) and [screenshots and API-call records](evidence/). CodeBuddy development usage and Tencent demo-call evidence are separate records.
  26→
  27→This is a local demonstration with synthetic trip data, not a connection to Ryde's production
  28→accounts or payment systems. It records decisions; it does not transfer money.
  29→
  30→## The challenge
  31→
  32→Ride-hailing platforms process thousands of dispute tickets daily: fare disputes, route deviations,
  33→property damage, safety incidents, no-show charges. They are subjective, emotionally charged, and
  34→currently resolved by humans reviewing GPS telemetry, chat logs, payment records and company policy
  35→by hand. The result is slow, expensive and inconsistent.
  36→
  37→The task is an autonomous multi-agent system that gathers evidence, builds both sides' cases, applies
  38→company policy and issues a fair ruling with a confidence score and a plain-language explanation.
  39→
  40→## Architecture
  41→
  42→Three core agents, all MVP-required:
  43→
  44→| Agent | Role |
  45→|---|---|
  46→| **Rider Advocate** | Builds the rider's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  47→| **Driver Advocate** | Builds the driver's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  48→| **Judge** | Weighs both cases, applies policy, rules, and explains the reasoning with a confidence score |
  49→
  50→Inter-agent communication must be **observable** — a judge needs to see how the agents exchange
  51→information and build their cases. That surface is a required deliverable, not a nice-to-have.
  52→
  53→The full walkthrough — components, lifecycle, gates, observability — is in
  54→[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md). The system on one page:
  55→
  56→```mermaid
  57→flowchart TD
  58→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  59→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  60→    A["Rider and driver intake forms"] --> B
  61→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  62→    CL --> C
  63→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  64→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  65→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  66→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  67→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  68→    E --> RA
  69→    E --> DA
  70→    RA --> S{"Questions for the party?"}
  71→    DA --> S
  72→    S -- "Yes, first round" --> O4["Needs info"]
  73→    O4 --> PA["Party answers follow-ups"]
  74→    PA -- "Fresh run with the answers" --> B
  75→    S -- "No" --> J
  76→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, NS-8, RD-5, RD-4"}
  77→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  78→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  79→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H
  80→    J -- "Model could not answer" --> H
  81→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]
  82→    J -.-> L
  83→    L -- "Embedded in the case file" --> K["Operator console"]
  84→```
  85→
  86→## Documents
  87→
  88→- [`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md) — the challenge statement, verbatim
  89→- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — architecture diagram and system description
  90→- [`docs/policy.md`](docs/policy.md) — the policy rule set the Judge applies, with per-rule provenance
  91→- [`docs/dataset.md`](docs/dataset.md) — the labelled corpus, its provenance and its limitations
  92→- [`docs/prompts.md`](docs/prompts.md) — how the prompts drive each agent, and what code checks after the model answers
  93→- [`docs/replay.md`](docs/replay.md) — the static replay of a recorded run: how it is exported and what it shows
  94→- [`docs/evidence-plan.md`](docs/evidence-plan.md) — development-process evidence rules
  95→- [`docs/tool-experiences.md`](docs/tool-experiences.md) — running log of how the development tools behaved
  96→- [`docs/build-briefs/`](docs/build-briefs/) — the brief each CodeBuddy build session worked from, kept as a record of the process
  97→- [`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md) — builder's entry point and project memory
  98→
  99→## Development tooling
 100→
 101→Built with Tencent Cloud **CodeBuddy**. The competition mandates proof of product usage, so
 102→development happens in the tool and evidence is captured as it occurs.
 103→
 104→## Run
 105→
 106→### One-click start
 107→
 108→Double-click **`start.command`** (macOS) or **`start.bat`** (Windows). That is the whole setup:
 109→Python 3.9 or newer is the only requirement, and no API key is needed, because the demo runs on
 110→the deterministic mock.
 111→
 112→The launcher picks a free port and opens `http://127.0.0.1:8000/start/` — the start page, which
 113→links to the party and operator surfaces. If port 8000 is busy it reuses a Ryde demo already running there;
 114→otherwise it tries 8001 to 8010 and uses the first free one. If you already started the demo
 115→yourself, the launcher reuses that copy as it is. The terminal window stays open while the demo
 116→runs: closing it (or pressing Ctrl+C in it) stops the server, while closing only the browser tab
 117→does not.
 118→
 119→A macOS ZIP download may need System Settings, Privacy & Security, **Open Anyway** for the first
 120→double-click. Windows SmartScreen may need **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
 121→
 122→### Manual start (fallback)
 123→
 124→No dependencies: it runs on a stock Python 3.9+ with the standard library only, using a
 125→deterministic mock in place of the LLM. Start the server and open the pages:
 126→
 127→```bash
 128→python3 -m app.server --llm mock
 129→```
 130→
 131→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/start/` is the entry page
 132→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` is the operator console (case files, the review queue, human decisions)
 133→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/` is the rider's dispute form, which links to the driver form and the status page
 134→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/driver-filing.html` is the driver's dispute form
 135→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/status.html` looks up a filing by its reference number
 136→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/driver.html` is the read-only sample driver account
 137→- `python3 -m app.server --llm mock --port 8011` serves the same pages on another port
 138→
 139→Use the port printed by the launcher if it is not 8000.
 140→
 141→### Live start (approved access only)
 142→
 143→Double-click **`start-live.command`** (macOS) or **`start-live.bat`** (Windows). This selects
 144→Tencent ADP explicitly, needs internet access and uses credits. Follow the
 145→[live-copy guide](docs/live-copy.md) to supply the private `.env.live` sidecar. No key is
 146→included in the public source.
 147→
 148→The live launcher uses port **8030** by default, opens the rider form rather than `/start/`,
 149→and prints the actual party, operator and status URLs. It refuses an occupied port and
 150→does not silently fall back to the mock. If private access is unavailable, use the standard
 151→keyless launchers instead and label the result as mock.
 152→
 153→To try the real model without keys, use the hosted [live AI site](https://ryde-dispute-live.edgeone.dev)
 154→listed under [Start here](#start-here).
 155→
 156→### Tests and command-line cases
 157→
 158→To run the tests and single cases from the command line:
 159→
 160→```bash
 161→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
 162→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0101
 163→python3 -m app.cli --pack organiser-style-v1 --dispute DISP-002
 164→```
 165→
 166→Live evaluation uses credits and requires approved access; it is not needed for the keyless demo.
 167→The evaluation harness replays every labelled case — `python3 -m app.eval --llm tencent --repeat 3` —
 168→and scores the rulings against the labels, answering a round-one stop and running it again.
 169→
 170→`--dispute` takes either a dispute id inside the selected pack or a path to a record file
 171→(`python3 -m app.cli --dispute data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/disputes/RD-0101.json`). The pack
 172→defaults to `dataset_pack` in `app/config.json`; `--pack` overrides it for one run.
 173→
 174→That prints the agent-to-agent event strip and the ruling, and writes the run's artifacts to
 175→`runs/<run_id>/`: `events.jsonl` (the observable traffic), `payloads/*.json` (the full payload
 176→behind each event) and `case_file.json` (evidence, both claims, resolution).
 177→
 178→The rider form is `/party/index.html`; the driver form is `/party/driver-filing.html`.
 179→Both use the shared form script and the same filing API. Save the reference number for
 180→`/party/status.html#reference-input`, which recovers questions and the current outcome.
 181→The rider demo list contains rider filings only. The read-only driver account at
 182→`/party/driver.html` is fixed to D-2009, including T-RD0109; filings on other sample drivers'
 183→trips need reference lookup and do not appear in that account. The forms are local demos,
 184→not signed-in accounts. Entering an amount is a request, not a payment.
 185→
 186→The corpus lives in two swappable packs under `data/packs/`: `ryde-synth-v1` (our 17 labelled
 187→cases, our record shape) and `organiser-style-v1` (the same 17 cases as twins in the organisers'
 188→shape, plus the organisers' own `DISP-002` verbatim). `RD-0103` is a deviation too small to matter. `NS-0203` is a driver who marked arrival 885 m
 189→from the pickup point. `RD-0109` is a remedy above the autonomous cap that the system refuses to
 190→issue on its own. `OS-0301` is an out-of-scope filing routed to human review without an LLM call. `docs/dataset.md` maps each case
 191→to what it tests; `<pack>/ground-truth.json` holds the expected outcomes, deliberately kept out
 192→of the records the agents see.
 193→
 194→Seven gates stand between a ruling and the parties, and **all seven are enforced in Python, not
 195→asked of the model in a prompt**. The confidence threshold is one of them, and so is ESC-4's SGD
 196→50 autonomous cap. ESC-2 withholds a route-case ruling when the deviation cannot be measured or the
 197→fare charged cannot be established. NS-6 withholds a contested no-show unless the ruling is a
 198→refund of exactly the fee for a low fee and a clean rider record. NS-8 withholds a no-show refund
 199→larger than the recorded fee, any compensation on a no-show case, or any refund whose fee the
 200→record cannot prove. RD-5 withholds a route ruling that refunds less than the overcharge the
 201→records prove. RD-4 withholds a route refund larger than the records prove the rider overpaid (a
 202→fixed fare paid as quoted proves nothing) and any compensation on a route case. Each gate
 203→withholds the ruling for a human; none of them rewrites what the Judge proposed.
 204→Try them:
 205→
 206→```bash
 207→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0109   # withheld: above the cap
 208→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0108   # withheld: no deviation to measure
 209→```
 210→
 211→**Mock by default.** The default provider is a deterministic mock. Its free-text fields (claim
 212→summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation) are prefixed `MOCK`; actions, amounts, rule IDs and
 213→evidence refs are not. A mock run is a plumbing demonstration, never a real ruling. The real model is
 214→Tencent Cloud ADP, one app per agent: put the three app keys in `.env` (see `.env.example`), then
 215→run `python3 -m app.server --llm tencent` or `python3 -m app.cli --llm tencent --dispute <id>`.
 216→
 217→## How this was built
 218→
 219→The code in `app/` and `ui/` was written in Tencent Cloud CodeBuddy. A planning agent wrote each
 220→session's brief and its failing tests first; CodeBuddy built until they passed, and the result was
 221→re-checked by running it, not by describing it. The screenshots in `evidence/` record those
 222→sessions as they happened.
